property_summary: Reference C never increases any account's balances when Deposit is called with msg.value < MinDeposit, but the mutant accepts msg.value == MinDeposit and therefore can increase balances for some inputs (msg.value == MinDeposit), violating the rule that deposits below or equal to threshold are ignored in reference—more precisely: reference only updates balances when msg.value > MinDeposit; mutant also updates when msg.value == MinDeposit.

For all callers and amounts, the reference contract never increases any stored balance when Deposit is called with msg.value <= MinDeposit (it only updates on msg.value > MinDeposit); the mutant changes the comparison to >= and therefore can increase a balance when msg.value == MinDeposit, violating this rule.

For every caller and amount, the reference contract only updates balances when msg.value > MinDeposit; the mutant changes the check to >= so it can update balances when msg.value == MinDeposit, violating the rule that deposits of exactly MinDeposit do not change balances in the reference.

Reference contract C never increases any stored balances when Deposit is called with msg.value == MinDeposit (it requires msg.value > MinDeposit); the mutant changes '>' to '>=' so a deposit of exactly MinDeposit can increase balances and thus violates this rule.

For any caller and any amount, calling Deposit with msg.value == MinDeposit does not change any stored balances in the reference C (only values > MinDeposit are accepted); the mutant accepts msg.value == MinDeposit and thus can increase balances for that exact amount.

For every caller and amount, deposits with msg.value > MinDeposit increase the caller's stored balance in the reference contract; the mutant inverts the gate so such larger deposits do not update balances, causing a discrepancy for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit the reference contract increases that caller's balances by the deposited amount (so balances[caller] after Deposit equals prior + msg.value), whereas the mutant (which uses msg.value < MinDeposit) fails to update balances for those amounts and thus can be distinguished.

For any caller and any deposit amount, if msg.value >= MinDeposit then C.Deposit updates that caller's balances by adding msg.value; the mutant inverts the gate (msg.value < MinDeposit) and therefore fails to update balances for some such amounts, so there exists a fuzzed (caller,amount) where balances differs after Deposit.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference C always increases balances(caller) by msg.value after Deposit; the mutant inverts the gate (msg.value < MinDeposit) and thus fails to update balances for such amounts, so there exist fuzzed inputs where balances differs.

For every caller and deposit amount, the reference contract only updates balances when msg.value > MinDeposit, so balances[k] either increases by msg.value for the depositor (and stays unchanged for others); the mutant inverts the comparison (msg.value < MinDeposit) and therefore there exist fuzzed (depositor, amount, key) where after Deposit the balances at some key differ between reference and mutant (specifically for amounts >= MinDeposit), violating the universal rule that large deposits increase the depositor's stored balance.

For any caller and any msg.value > MinDeposit, the reference contract C always increases balances[caller] by exactly msg.value (and thus balances[caller] after Deposit equals old + msg.value); the mutant that removed the overflow check can cause balances at some address to differ (due to wraparound) for some fuzzed msg.value, so there exists an input where balances diverge between reference and mutant.

For any caller and any msg.value > MinDeposit, the reference contract C guarantees balances[caller] increases by exactly msg.value (no wraparound), whereas the mutant (removing the require) can overflow and make balances[caller] not equal old + msg.value for some fuzzed msg.value, so there exists an input where balances diverge.

For every caller and deposit value > MinDeposit, the reference contract C ensures that balances[caller] either increases monotonically (i.e., new balances[caller] >= old balances[caller]) because the reference checks for overflow, whereas the mutant that removed the require allows an arithmetic wraparound so there exist deposit values that make balances[caller] become smaller than before (wrap), breaking the monotonicity.

For any depositor address a and any deposit value v > MinDeposit, the reference contract C guarantees that no account's balances mapping decreases as a result of that deposit (i.e., for all keys k, C.balances(k) after deposit is >= C.balances(k) before the deposit); removing the overflow check in the mutant can cause some key's stored balance to wrap and decrease for some fuzzed v, violating this global non-decrease property.

For any depositor address and deposit value > MinDeposit, calling Deposit never changes the balance of any OTHER address (i.e., C.balances(k) for k != depositor remains equal before and after); removing the overflow check can cause an overflow that corrupts storage slot layout and make some other key's balance change for some fuzzed inputs, so the mutant can violate this property.

For every caller and deposit amount > MinDeposit, the reference contract always records the Deposit log after increasing balances (so balances getter reflects the deposited amount when read after Deposit); the mutant that logs first can make the recorded log reflect a balance that does not include the deposit (i.e. balances differs for some key), so reading balances after Deposit can differ between reference and mutant.

After any successful Deposit by an address A of amount v > MinDeposit, the contract's balances(A) equals the sum of prior balances(A) plus v (i.e., Deposit always increments the caller's balance); the mutant that logs before updating can produce a state where balances differs for some caller after Deposit.

For every caller and deposit amount > MinDeposit, after Deposit completes the reference contract's balances(caller) increases by exactly the sent amount (i.e., balances == prior + value); the mutant that logs before updating can produce a different balances for some input because the log observation order may expose the pre-update value.

For any depositor A and any deposit value v > MinDeposit, if a different address K reads the latest log entry after A.Deposit(v) then the reference contract's balances(K) equals the post-deposit stored value (i.e., reading balances after Deposit always reflects the state update), whereas the mutant that logs before updating can produce a situation where the log records pre-update state and thus some observed balances(K) differ — we encode this by making K read balances(K) after Deposit and asserting balances(K) equals c.balances(K) (identity) on the reference but the mutant can produce a mismatch for some fuzzed K and v when logs are observed via the reading address); concretely we assert that a read of c.balances(k) after Deposit returns the same value as the contract's internal balances getter (i.e., it's consistent) for all inputs — the mutant can break consistency when logging occurs before the state update and an external reader uses the log to infer state.

For any depositor and any deposit value > MinDeposit, after Deposit returns the contract's balances for every address equals the stored mapping (i.e., reading c.balances(addr) after Deposit yields the updated mapping); the mutant that logs before updating can cause c.balances(addr) to not reflect the intended post-deposit mapping for some addr/value.

For any caller and deposit amount > MinDeposit, calling Deposit preserves all other accounts' balances (only the caller's balance may increase by the deposit under reference C); the mutant overwrites balances[msg.sender] = msg.value which can incorrectly zero or change other keys compared to the expected additive behavior, so there exists inputs where balances(k) differs.

For any caller A and deposit value v > MinDeposit, the reference implementation increases only A's balance by v (balances(A) after = balances(A) before + v) and leaves every other account K != A unchanged; the mutant can overwrite balances[A] = v which can change balances for other keys relative to the reference, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount > MinDeposit, calling Deposit never changes balances of any other address K != depositor (reference preserves other keys); the mutant can overwrite mapping data and thus will for some inputs make balances(K) differ.

For any depositor A and deposit value v > MinDeposit, the reference contract only updates balances[A] (incrementing it by v) and never sets any other mapping slot; the mutant that assigns balances[msg.sender] = msg.value can overwrite a different mapping slot when storage collision occurs (e.g., via a crafted depositor address whose storage layout causes keccak collision), so there exist inputs where balances(k) differs after Deposit.

For any depositor address A and deposit value v > MinDeposit, the reference contract preserves the invariant that for every address K != A, balances(K) remains equal to its prior value (Deposit only increments the caller's slot); the mutant that writes balances[msg.sender]=msg.value can change a different mapping slot via storage aliasing when callers collide, so there exist fuzzed addresses and amounts that make balances(K) differ.

For any caller address A and any deposit amount v > MinDeposit, calling Deposit will (in the reference) always credit balances[A] with v (i.e., balances[A] increases when Deposit is called by A with value > MinDeposit); the mutant adds require(msg.sender!=address(0)) so a call that originates from address(0) will be rejected and balances[0x0] will not be increased, violating the universal property.

For any caller A and any value v > MinDeposit, calling Deposit succeeds and increases C.balances(A) in the reference; the mutant rejects calls when msg.sender == address(0) and thus can make balances(0) not increase (or the call revert), breaking the universal rule for that adversarial caller.

For any caller address A and any deposit amount v > MinDeposit, calling Deposit succeeds (does not revert) and increases balances(A) by v in the reference; the mutant adds require(msg.sender != address(0)) so a call originating from a contract that forwards with msg.sender == address(0) (a precompile-like proxy) can be rejected or not credited, breaking this property.

For any nonzero deposit value > MinDeposit and any caller address A, calling Deposit should increase C.balances(A) (i.e. Deposit credits the msg.sender); the mutant adds require(msg.sender != address(0)) so a call that arrives with msg.sender == address(0) will not be credited, violating this universal property for that special caller scenario.

For any depositor address A and any value v > MinDeposit, calling Deposit increases C.balances(A) in the reference implementation; the mutant adds require(msg.sender != address(0)) so a specially crafted proxy contract that manages to invoke C.Deposit while making C.see msg.sender == address(0) (simulated by a contract that self-destructs after setting its code to zero via a delegatecall pattern is not possible on EVM, so instead we target the observable difference by using a helper that calls C.Deposit but uses an intermediate contract whose address is 0 when the reference would accept a deposit credited to the helper's address while the mutant rejects it — equivalently, the reference allows deposits credited to any caller including a contract helper address, whereas the mutant rejects deposits that present msg.sender == address(0); thus the universal rule is: any successful Deposit call with value>MinDeposit increases balances(caller) — the mutant can cause a Deposit to revert or not credit when the intermediate yields msg.sender == address(0))

For any caller and any msg.value > MinDeposit, calling Deposit increases the caller's recorded balance by msg.value (and thus c.balances(caller) >= previous + msg.value); the mutant that flips the condition to msg.value <= MinDeposit prevents such increases for values > MinDeposit and thus violates this rule for some fuzzed msg.value.

For any caller and any deposit amount greater than MinDeposit, the reference contract always increases the caller's stored balance by that amount; the mutant that accepts only deposits <= MinDeposit will fail this for some fuzzed amounts > MinDeposit.

For any caller and any deposit amount strictly greater than MinDeposit, calling Deposit should succeed and increase the caller's recorded balance by that amount; the mutant that flips the condition to msg.value <= MinDeposit will reject/inhibit such larger deposits and thus violate this property for some fuzzed amounts.

For any caller A and any deposit amount v where v >= MinDeposit+1 wei (i.e. strictly greater than MinDeposit), calling Deposit with value v increases c.balances(A) by exactly v; the mutant that flips the condition to msg.value <= MinDeposit will fail to increase balances for such v, so there exist fuzzed inputs (A,v) that make the mutant violate this rule.

For any caller and any deposit amount strictly greater than MinDeposit, calling Deposit succeeds and increases the caller's recorded balance by that amount; the mutant that flips the condition to msg.value <= MinDeposit will not increase balances for some such amounts and thus violate this rule.

For any caller and any deposited msg.value, reference C only increases a caller's balance when msg.value > MinDeposit (1 ether); the mutant removes that guard and therefore can increase balances for msg.value <= MinDeposit, violating the rule for some inputs.

For all callers and amounts, the reference contract only increases balances on Deposit when msg.value > MinDeposit (1 ether); the mutant removes that guard and can increase balances for msg.value <= MinDeposit, so the invariant 'after Deposit, balances[actor] increases iff msg.value > MinDeposit' is violated by the mutant for some fuzzed msg.value ≤ MinDeposit.

For every caller and deposit amount, the reference C only increases the caller's balances when msg.value > MinDeposit; the mutant removes that guard and therefore for some msg.value <= MinDeposit will increase balances (violating that rule).

For every caller and deposit amount <= MinDeposit the reference contract leaves the caller's balance unchanged after Deposit (no balance increase), whereas the mutant erroneously increases balances for some such small deposits.

For every caller and deposit amount <= MinDeposit, calling Deposit does not change the caller's recorded balance in the reference contract; the mutant removed the guard and can erroneously increase the balance for some small deposits.

After any successful Deposit call by an account with value > MinDeposit, the latest logged History entry (History[last].Val and History[last].Sender and History[last].Data) must reflect the new balance change order: specifically, in the correct contract the logged message appears after balances has been increased so that History[last].Val equals the deposited amount and History[last].Sender equals depositor — this breaks in the mutant which logs before updating balances causing the observable sequence (log vs balance) to be inconsistent for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount > MinDeposit, after Deposit returns the contract's logged last History entry (LastMsg via History) must reflect a balance at least as large as the deposit (i.e., the depositor's stored balances >= deposited amount) — the mutant that logs before updating balances can produce a History entry inconsistent with the updated balances, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount > MinDeposit, if Deposit succeeds then the contract's recorded last History entry (History[last].Val and .Sender) must match the deposit call's sender and amount AND the depositor's stored balances must be >= the deposited amount — the mutant that logs before updating balances can produce a History entry that does not reflect the post-Deposit balances, violating this relation for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount > MinDeposit, after Deposit returns the logged History entry's Sender must equal the depositor address (i.e., the log records the actual caller); the mutant that logs before updating balances can still produce a History entry but the distinguishing behavior is that the log's Sender must always equal msg.sender — the mutant doesn't change Sender but reordering can be detected when using a re-entrant attacker that changes balances during Deposit, so requiring the log's Sender equal the depositor exposes inconsistencies when adversary re-enters.

For any depositor and deposit amount > MinDeposit, if a depositor's Deposit call triggers a failing transfer to the depositor (so the log call happens but the external call reverts), the correct contract will only append the History entry after balances is increased (so after Deposit returns the stored balances >= previous balance), whereas the mutant that logs before updating balances can record a History entry that reflects the deposit happened earlier than the balances update; thus there exists an adversarial re-entrant callee which makes the ordering observable and the mutant will violate the invariant that after Deposit returns, the History's last entry corresponds to a state where balances[depositor] >= previous balance + deposited amount — the correct contract satisfies this for all inputs but the mutant fails for some inputs.

For any caller and any withdrawal amount, the original contract never allows CashOut to reduce the contract balance below the caller's pre-withdrawal balance (i.e., CashOut only succeeds when _am <= balances[msg.sender]); the mutant that accepts all _am values can attempt over-withdrawals that either revert or change address(c).balance differently, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any amount, CashOut never allows the contract to send more than the caller's recorded balance: if the call succeeds, address(c).balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount and the caller's recorded balance is never allowed to go negative; the mutant that permits _am > balances[msg.sender] can either revert or cause address(c).balance to decrease by more than the caller's recorded balance for some inputs.

For any caller and any amount, if CashOut returns (does not revert) then the contract's balance decreases by exactly the amount sent and the caller's recorded balance after the call equals its prior balance minus that amount; the mutant that allows _am > balances[msg.sender] can either revert or cause a mismatch (contract balance change or stored balance) for some inputs.
